 First Alert: Freezing temperatures Friday & Saturday morning 
 Slushy lake effect snow will stay in Northwest, IN 
 Freezing temperatures and lake-effect snow showers are expected Friday and Saturday across parts of Michiana. By Andrew Whitmyer Published : Sep. 2, 2025 at 6:31 PM EDT | Updated : 31 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Get ready for a chilly stretch, Michiana! Friday and Saturday are First Alert Weather Days as the season’s first below-freezing temperatures arrive and lake-effect snow showers develop.
 The best chance for accumulating snow Friday morning will be in northwest Indiana. As winds shift Saturday, some lake-effect snow showers could reach more of Michiana, including the South Bend and Elkhart area.
 Friday: First Alert Weather Day for the season’s first below freezing air 
 Friday morning is expected to bring our first below-freezing temperatures of the fall season. Make sure the kids have their winter jackets ready for the bus stop!
 Winds out of the north will keep lake-effect snow mainly in northwest Indiana, where a few communities could see a few inches of slushy accumulation Friday morning. Most of that snow is expected on grass, rooftops and car windshields.
 Friday will remain cold, with highs only in the low 40s. Lake-effect rain and snow showers are possible in affected areas.
 Saturday First Alert Weather Day: Another freezing morning and more lake-effect showers 
 Saturday is also a First Alert Weather Day. Temperatures will again fall below freezing overnight into Saturday morning, potentially reaching the mid- to upper 20s where there are breaks in the clouds.
 Winds will likely shift from the north to the northwest, allowing some lake-effect snow showers to move into Michiana Saturday morning. A few lake-effect rain showers could linger in some areas Saturday afternoon as temperatures climb into the low to mid-40s.
 Notre Dame game day 
 Heading to the Notre Dame-Boston College game Saturday? Bundle up! Snow showers are possible during tailgating, with temperatures around 38°. A few rain showers could be around for the 3:30 p.m. kickoff, when temperatures should be near 44°. Conditions are expected to turn dry during the game, with temperatures falling back into the upper 30s by the end.
 Sunday and beyond 
 Sunday looks dry and chilly, with a high in the mid-40s. Temperatures will gradually warm next week, reaching the 50s and potentially around 60° by next weekend.
 A bigger pattern change may arrive during Thanksgiving week, bringing a more prolonged stretch of cold weather and, yes, more chances for snow. We’ll keep you updated as the forecast comes into focus.
